hints.title: Distinct User Category Association
hints.text: Extract unique category purchases per customer before joining.

hints.title: Pairwise Category Comparison
hints.text: Join the distinct customer category dataset with itself on identical customer identifiers enforcing strictly ascending category ordering.

hints.title: Threshold Filtering and Ordering
hints.text: Count distinct customers per category pair, retain pairs with customer count at least 3, and order by count descending then category names ascending.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH UserCategories AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT 
        p.user_id, 
        i.category
    FROM ProductPurchases p
    JOIN ProductInfo i 
      ON p.product_id = i.product_id
),
CategoryPairs AS (
    SELECT 
        uc1.user_id,
        uc1.category AS category1,
        uc2.category AS category2
    FROM UserCategories uc1
    JOIN UserCategories uc2 
      ON uc1.user_id = uc2.user_id 
     AND uc1.category < uc2.category
),
PairCustomerCounts AS (
    SELECT 
        category1, 
        category2, 
        COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customer_count
    FROM CategoryPairs
    GROUP BY category1, category2
)
SELECT 
    category1, 
    category2, 
    customer_count
FROM PairCustomerCounts
WHERE customer_count >= 3
ORDER BY customer_count DESC, 
         category1 ASC, 
         category2 ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Group aggregation with self-join on deduplicated customer categories.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Joining full purchase tables without category deduplication counts duplicate purchases by the same buyer multiple times.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: CTE deduplication minimizes rows fed into the self-join.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use CTEs or subqueries to deduplicate categories per customer and avoid self-pairings.

import pandas as pd

def find_category_recommendation_pairs(product_purchases: pd.DataFrame, product_info: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = product_purchases.merge(product_info, on="product_id", how="inner")
    user_cats = merged[["user_id", "category"]].drop_duplicates()
    pairs = user_cats.merge(user_cats, on="user_id", suffixes=("1", "2"))
    pairs = pairs[pairs["category1"] < pairs["category2"]]
    grouped = pairs.groupby(["category1", "category2"])["user_id"].nunique().reset_index()
    grouped.rename(columns={"user_id": "customer_count"}, inplace=True)
    filtered = grouped[grouped["customer_count"] >= 3]
    return filtered.sort_values(by=["customer_count", "category1", "category2"], ascending=[False, True, True])
